title: Medieval romance and chivalry: quests, courtly love and Sir Orfeo
examples: What is the story of Sir Orfeo?

explain.say: In Beowulf a hero fights for his people and dies. In a medieval romance a knight rides out for love or honour and meets fairies, giants and enchanted castles. The board shows the difference. Romance comes from romanz, stories told in French instead of Latin.

draw.text: Medieval romance and chivalry: quests, courtly love and Sir Orfeo

explain.say: Look at the 1170s. The French poet Chretien de Troyes wrote of Lancelot, who serves Queen Guinevere as a devoted lover. In 1883 the scholar Gaston Paris called this ideal courtly love: a knight humbly serving a lady, often in secret. Is that love, or a performance?

explain.say: Chivalry was the knight's code. See the four groups: prowess, loyalty, courtesy and largesse, meaning generosity. Real medieval warfare was far more brutal than the ideal, and romances often test the gap. Which virtue still matters today?

Here is an English romance, Sir Orfeo, from around 1300. It retells the Greek myth of Orpheus. The fairy king steals Queen Heurodis, and Orfeo wanders the wild for ten years with his harp, then plays so well he wins her back. Why give the sad old myth a happy ending?

explain.say: Look at the last panel: home in disguise, Orfeo finds his steward loyal, so the kingdom is whole again. Romance never died; Cervantes mocked it in 1605, and fantasy films still follow it. Lovely work. Challenge: name a modern film with a quest, a test and a magic helper.

faq.a: A story in verse or prose about knights, quests, love and marvels, first written in French in the 1100s and later in English. Sir Gawain and Sir Orfeo are famous English examples.
asks: Romance genre in the Middle Ages

faq.a: An ideal of love in medieval romance and lyric: a knight serves a noble lady with devotion, humility and often secrecy. The term was coined by Gaston Paris in 1883.
The code of the medieval knight: prowess in arms, loyalty, courtesy, generosity and faith. Romances present it as an ideal and often test its limits.
asks: What was the code of chivalry?

faq.a: A Middle English Breton lay from around 1300 that retells the Orpheus myth. King Orfeo wins back his wife Heurodis from the fairy king with his harping, and returns home.

faq.q: How is romance different from epic?
faq.a: Epic centres on war, the fate of a people and heroic death. Romance centres on an individual knight's quest, love, courtesy and the marvellous, and usually ends happily.

facts: Chretien de Troyes wrote his Arthurian romances in the 1170s and 1180s.
Gaston Paris coined the term amour courtois, courtly love, in 1883.
Sir Orfeo survives in the Auchinleck manuscript, copied in the 1330s.
